source.title: My Things
source.description: Identifica pertenencias y reconoce de quién son los objetos con my, your, his y her.

pronunciation.activity: Practicar el sonido inicial y repetir

grammar.focus: Adjetivos posesivos: my / your / his / her
grammar.explanation: Los posesivos indican de quién es algo. «My» significa mi, «your» tu, «his» su de él y «her» su de ella. El posesivo va delante del objeto: «my bag», «his book», «her toy».
grammar.model: This is my bag. It is her book.
grammar.practice: Relaciona a cada persona con su objeto y selecciona el posesivo adecuado.

items.prompt: You talk about your own pencil. Choose the word.
items.es: My se usa para hablar de nuestras cosas.

items.prompt: You talk to a friend about the friend's bag. Choose the word.
items.es: Your significa tu o tus.

items.prompt: A boy has a book. Choose the phrase.
items.es: His indica que el libro pertenece a él.

items.prompt: A girl has a toy. Choose the phrase.
items.es: Her indica que el juguete pertenece a ella.

source.readingText: This is Ben's school bag. His book is blue and his pencil is green. Mia has a red bag. Her book is small. “This is my toy,” says Ben. Mia points to her doll and says, “This is my toy.” The children put their things on the table.

readingQuestions.question: What does Ben call his toy?
Where do the children put their things?
Which possessive shows that something belongs to Ben?
Which possessive shows that something belongs to Mia?

source.listeningScript: Teacher: Is this your bag, Ben? Ben: Yes, it is my bag. Teacher: And is this your book? Ben: No, it is her book. It is Mia's. Mia: This is my pencil. Teacher: And what is that? Mia: It is his toy. Teacher: Very good. Put your things on the table, please.

listeningQuestions.question: Who speaks to Ben and Mia?
What does Ben say about the bag?
What does Mia say is hers?
Which possessive does Ben use for his bag?
Which possessive does the teacher use when speaking to Ben?
Where must they put their things?

source.title: Whose Is It?
source.description: Pregunta de quién es un objeto y responde con posesivos en diálogos breves.

pronunciation.activity: Escuchar el sonido inicial y repetir
Unir las palabras con ritmo natural

grammar.explanation: Usamos «Whose…?» para preguntar de quién es un objeto. Podemos responder «It’s my…», «It’s your…», «It’s his…» o «It’s her…». El posesivo va delante del nombre del objeto.
grammar.model: Whose pencil is it? It's his pencil.
grammar.practice: Completa un diálogo sobre objetos perdidos con la pregunta y el posesivo adecuados.

items.prompt: Choose the question “¿De quién es el lápiz?”.
items.es: Whose pregunta de quién es algo.

items.prompt: A boy owns the bag. Choose the phrase.
items.es: His indica que pertenece a él.

items.prompt: A girl owns the pencil. Choose the phrase.
items.es: Her indica que pertenece a ella.

items.prompt: Complete: Whose book is ___?
items.es: La pregunta modelo termina con is it?

source.readingText: After class, a pencil is on the floor. Ben asks, “Whose pencil is it?” Mia says, “It's my pencil.” Then they find a blue bag. “Whose bag is it?” asks Ben. The teacher says, “It's her bag. It belongs to Anna.” Anna comes back and takes her bag. Ben and Mia help their friend.

readingQuestions.question: When do Ben and Mia find the pencil?
Who says the bag belongs to Anna?
What does Anna do when she comes back?

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Welcome to Lost and Found. A pencil is on the desk. Whose pencil is it? Girl: It's my pencil. Presenter: Thank you. Now, a blue bag. Whose bag is it? Boy: It's her bag. It is Lucy's. Presenter: And this book? Girl: It's his book. It belongs to Tom. Presenter: Thank you for helping us!

listeningQuestions.question: What does the boy say about the bag?
Which possessive does the girl use for Tom's book?

source.title: I Have Got
source.description: Expresa posesión con have got y reconoce las formas afirmativas más frecuentes.

grammar.focus: Have got afirmativo: I've got / you've got / he's got / she's got
grammar.explanation: Usamos «have got» para decir que tenemos algo. Las formas cortas son «I’ve got» y «you’ve got». Con «he» y «she» usamos «has got», que se contrae como «he’s got» y «she’s got». Después ponemos el objeto: «I’ve got a book».
grammar.model: I've got a book. She's got a toy.
grammar.practice: Elige have got o has got según la persona que tiene el objeto.

items.prompt: Choose the correct phrase with I.
items.es: Con I usamos I've got.

items.prompt: Choose the correct phrase with he.
items.es: Con he usamos he's got.

items.prompt: Complete: She ___ got a toy.
items.es: Con she la forma completa es has got.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
items.es: Con you usamos you've got.

source.readingText: Sam has a new blue ball. He says, “I've got a ball.” His sister Mia has a red toy. She says, “I've got a toy.” Their friend Ben has a book. He says, “I've got a book.” The children put their things on the table. They are happy with their new things.

readingQuestions.question: What does Sam say he has got?
Where do the children put their things?
What language pattern do they practise?

source.listeningScript: Interviewer: Hello, Alex. What have you got? Alex: I've got a red ball. Interviewer: And your sister? Alex: She's got a book. Interviewer: What about your brother? Alex: He's got a toy car. Interviewer: Have you got a bag? Alex: Yes, I've got a blue bag, too.

listeningQuestions.question: Which phrase does Alex use for himself?

source.title: Have You Got…?
source.description: Pregunta si alguien tiene un objeto y responde con respuestas cortas afirmativas o negativas.

pronunciation.activity: Unir la respuesta con ritmo natural

grammar.focus: Have got: preguntas y respuestas breves
grammar.explanation: Preguntamos si alguien tiene algo con «Have you got…?». Respondemos «Yes, I have» si lo tenemos y «No, I haven’t» si no lo tenemos. La pregunta va seguida del objeto: «Have you got a pen?»
grammar.model: Have you got a pen? Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
grammar.practice: Lee la pregunta y elige la respuesta que coincide con la situación.

items.prompt: Choose the correct question.
items.es: La pregunta empieza con Have you got…?

items.prompt: You have a book. Choose the answer.
items.es: Si lo tienes, respondes Yes, I have.

items.prompt: You do not have a pencil. Choose the answer.
items.es: Si no lo tienes, respondes No, I haven't.

items.prompt: Complete: Have you ___ a bag?
items.es: La pregunta completa es Have you got…?

source.readingText: It is English class. The teacher asks Mia, “Have you got a pencil?” Mia says, “Yes, I have.” Then the teacher asks Ben, “Have you got a ruler?” Ben says, “No, I haven't.” He has got a pen instead. Mia has got a blue bag and Ben has got a green book. The class is ready to write.

readingQuestions.question: What does the teacher ask Mia about?
What does the teacher ask Ben about?
What are the children ready to do?
What language pattern does the class practise?
readingQuestions.answer: Have you got? and short answers
options: Have you got? and short answers

source.listeningScript: Listen to a story in the classroom. The teacher asks Tom, “Have you got a book?” Tom says, “Yes, I have.” Then she asks Lucy, “Have you got a ruler?” Lucy says, “No, I haven't.” She has got a pencil. The teacher asks, “Have you got a bag, Tom?” “Yes, I have. It is blue,” he says. They start the lesson.

listeningQuestions.question: Who does the teacher ask first?
What does the teacher ask Lucy about?
What does the teacher ask Tom about next?
What do the pupils do at the end?

source.title: Food I Like
source.theme: Repaso integrado de comida y gustos
source.description: Expresa preferencias sobre alimentos y responde a preguntas sencillas con Do you like…?

pronunciation.activity: Unir las palabras con ritmo natural
Escuchar el grupo inicial y repetir

grammar.focus: I like / I don't like / Do you like…?
grammar.explanation: Usamos «I like…» para decir que algo nos gusta y «I don’t like…» para decir que no nos gusta. Para preguntar a otra persona usamos «Do you like…?». Podemos responder «Yes, I do» o «No, I don’t».
grammar.model: Do you like apples? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
grammar.practice: Pregunta sobre un alimento y selecciona una respuesta de gusto.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
items.es: Con I usamos like sin -s.

items.prompt: Which question asks about a food preference?
items.es: La pregunta se forma con Do you like…?

items.prompt: You like carrots. Choose the answer.
items.es: Yes, I do responde afirmativamente a Do you like…?

items.prompt: You do not like milk. Choose the sentence.
items.es: La forma negativa con I es I don't like.

source.readingText: At lunch, Mia and Ben talk about food. Mia likes apples and carrots, but she doesn't like bananas. Ben likes bananas and bread. He doesn't like carrots. Mum asks, “Do you like milk?” Mia says, “Yes, I do.” Ben says, “No, I don't.” They have different tastes.

readingQuestions.question: When do Mia and Ben talk about food?
Which fruit does Mia not like?
What does the text say about Mia and Ben?
options: They like exactly the same food

source.listeningScript: Dad: Do you like apples, Lucy? Lucy: Yes, I do. Dad: Do you like bananas? Lucy: No, I don't. Dad: What about carrots? Lucy: I like carrots. Dad: And milk? Lucy: Yes, I like milk. Dad: Great. I like apples and bananas. Lucy: We like some different foods!

listeningQuestions.question: Do Dad and Lucy like exactly the same foods?

source.title: Animal Descriptions
source.theme: Descripciones simples con to be y adjetivos
source.description: Combina el nombre de un animal con su tamaño, velocidad y una característica sencilla.

pronunciation.activity: Unir las palabras con ritmo natural

grammar.focus: It is… / It has got… / It can… (descripción inicial)
grammar.explanation: Para describir un animal podemos decir «It is…» y añadir una característica: big, small, fast o slow. También podemos reconocer «It has got…» para nombrar una parte del cuerpo y «It can…» para una capacidad: «It can run».
grammar.model: It is big. It has got a tail. It can run.
grammar.practice: Lee tres pistas sobre un animal y elige la descripción que coincide.

items.prompt: Choose the correct description.
items.es: Con it usamos is.

items.prompt: Complete: It ___ got a tail.
items.es: El modelo con it es has got.

items.prompt: Which word means “lento/a”?
items.es: Slow significa lento.

items.prompt: Choose the correct ability phrase.
items.es: Después de can usamos el verbo base.

source.readingText: At the zoo, a big elephant walks slowly. It has got a long nose and a tail. A small monkey is in a tree. It can jump fast. A bird is small and it has got wings. It can fly. The turtle is slow, but it can swim. The children look at all the animals.

readingQuestions.question: What has the elephant got?
readingQuestions.answer: A long nose and a tail
options: A long nose and a tail

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Welcome to Animal Descriptions. First, the elephant. It is big and slow. It has got a long nose. Next, the monkey. It is small and fast. It can jump. Look at the bird. It has got wings and it can fly. Finally, the turtle. It is slow. It has got a shell and it can swim.

source.title: My Clothes and Colors
source.theme: Repaso integrado de ropa y descripciones
source.description: Describe prendas y colores con frases modelo y la expresión I'm wearing.

pronunciation.activity: Repetir la contracción con ritmo natural
Unir las palabras con ritmo natural

grammar.explanation: Usamos «I’m wearing…» para decir qué ropa llevamos puesta. Después ponemos la prenda: «I’m wearing a hat». Para decir el color usamos «It’s…»: «It’s blue». El color va antes del nombre cuando describimos una prenda: «a blue hat».
grammar.model: I'm wearing a blue hat. It's blue.
grammar.practice: Mira la ropa de la persona y completa la descripción con prenda y color.

items.prompt: Choose the correct phrase.
items.es: La fórmula del currículo es I'm wearing…

items.prompt: Complete: It's ___. (azul)
items.es: Blue significa azul.

items.prompt: Choose the correct word order.
items.es: El color aparece antes del nombre.

items.prompt: Choose the sentence about shoes.
items.es: Usamos I'm wearing + color + prenda.

source.readingText: Look at the school photo. Ben is wearing a red coat and blue shoes. Mia is wearing a blue hat. Her coat is red. Tom is wearing black shoes and a green T-shirt. The children smile for the photo. They are wearing different clothes and colours.

readingQuestions.question: What is Ben wearing?
readingQuestions.answer: A red coat and blue shoes
options: A red coat and blue shoes
A blue hat and red shoes

readingQuestions.question: What is Mia wearing on her head?
Who is wearing a red coat?
Are the children wearing the same clothes?
What do the children do for the photo?

source.listeningScript: Interviewer: Hello, Lucy. What are you wearing today? Lucy: I'm wearing a blue hat and a red coat. Interviewer: What colour are your shoes? Lucy: They're black. Interviewer: And your friend? Lucy: Ben is wearing a green T-shirt and blue shoes. Interviewer: Thank you, Lucy!

listeningQuestions.question: What is Lucy wearing on her head?
Who is wearing a green T-shirt?
Which phrase does Lucy use to describe her clothes?
What does the interviewer say at the end?

source.title: Around the House – Review
source.theme: Repaso acumulativo de casa, objetos y ubicación
source.description: Repasa habitaciones, muebles y preposiciones para describir una escena del hogar.

pronunciation.activity: Unir las dos partes y repetir
Unir las palabras con ritmo natural
Unir las palabras con ritmo natural

grammar.explanation: Repasamos «There is» para una cosa y «There are» para varias. Para indicar la posición usamos preposiciones como «in», «on», «under» y «next to». Observa primero cuántos objetos hay y dónde están.
grammar.model: There is a sofa. The chair is next to the table.
grammar.practice: Completa una descripción de una casa eligiendo singular/plural y la preposición adecuada.
grammar.order: The chair is next to the table.
final: The chair is next to the table.
The chair are next to the table.
The chair is the table next to.

items.prompt: Complete: There ___ a sofa.
items.es: Sofa es singular.

items.prompt: Complete: There ___ two bedrooms.
items.es: Two bedrooms es plural.

items.prompt: The cat is ___ the table. It is below it.
items.es: Under indica que está debajo.

items.prompt: The chair is ___ the sofa. It is beside it.
items.es: Next to significa al lado de.

source.readingText: Welcome to our house. There is a sofa in the living room. There are two chairs next to the table. In the kitchen, there is a small table. There is a blue bag under the chair. In the bedroom, there is a bed and a lamp. The house is tidy and comfortable.

readingQuestions.question: How many chairs are next to the table?
Which preposition describes the bag's position?
Is the house tidy or messy?
What does the text describe?
readingQuestions.answer: A house and where things are
options: A house and where things are

source.listeningScript: Come into our home. There is a sofa in the living room. There are two chairs next to the table. In the kitchen, there is a table and four cups. Look under the chair. There is a blue bag. In the bedroom, there is a bed. The lamp is on the table. Our home is ready for visitors.

listeningQuestions.question: What place does the story describe?
What is in the living room?
How many chairs are next to the table?
What is the home ready for?
Which grammar is reviewed?
listeningQuestions.answer: There is / There are and prepositions
options: There is / There are and prepositions

source.title: Let's Ask Questions
source.theme: Preguntas básicas con what, who, where
source.description: Comprende preguntas con what, who y where y elige respuestas adecuadas.

pronunciation.activity: Escuchar la h muda y repetir
Unir las palabras con ritmo natural

grammar.explanation: «What» pregunta por una cosa o información: «What is it?». «Who» pregunta por una persona: «Who is she?». «Where» pregunta por un lugar o posición: «Where is the school?». Escucha la palabra inicial para saber qué información se pide.
grammar.model: What is it? Who is she? Where is the school?
grammar.practice: Relaciona cada pregunta con el tipo de respuesta que necesita.

items.prompt: Which question asks about a person?
items.es: Who pregunta quién es una persona.

items.prompt: Which question asks about a thing?
items.es: What pregunta qué es una cosa.

items.prompt: Which question asks about a place?
items.es: Where pregunta dónde está un lugar.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ is your teacher?
items.es: Preguntamos por la persona con Who.

source.readingText: In the classroom, Ben asks three questions. He points to a pencil and asks, “What is it?” Mia says, “It's a pencil.” Then Ben points to the teacher and asks, “Who is she?” Mia says, “She is Miss Green.” Finally, Ben asks, “Where is the book?” Mia points to the table. The book is on the table.

readingQuestions.question: What object does Ben point to first?
What question does Ben ask about the pencil?
What does Mia say the object is?
Who does Ben point to next?
What question does he ask about the teacher?
What question does Ben ask last?
Which question word asks about a place?

source.listeningScript: Teacher: Let's ask questions. Ben, what is it? Ben: It is a book. Teacher: Good. Mia, who is he? Mia: He is Mr Brown. Teacher: And where is the pencil? Mia: It is in the bag. Teacher: Very good. What asks about a thing, who asks about a person, and where asks about a place.

listeningQuestions.question: What does the teacher ask Ben about?
Which question does the teacher ask about a person?
Which word asks about a thing?
Which word asks about a person?
Which word asks about a place?

source.title: Pre-A1 Grand Adventure
source.description: Consolida vocabulario y estructuras esenciales antes de comenzar el nivel A1.

pronunciation.activity: Unir las palabras con ritmo natural
Escuchar la h muda y repetir

grammar.focus: Repaso integrado: TO BE, can, likes, there is/are y preposiciones
grammar.explanation: Esta misión reúne estructuras que ya has practicado. Usa «It is…» para describir, «It can…» para capacidades, «I like…» para gustos, «There is / There are» para decir qué hay y las preposiciones para indicar dónde está algo. No necesitas aprender una regla nueva: combina modelos conocidos.
grammar.model: It is a fox. It can run. There is a tree. The ball is under the tree.
grammar.practice: Lee cada pequeña situación y combina la estructura que ya conoces.

items.prompt: Choose the correct description.
items.es: Repaso de It is + nombre.

items.prompt: Choose the correct ability sentence.
items.es: Después de can usamos el verbo base.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about a tree.
items.es: There is se usa para una cosa.

items.prompt: The ball is below the table. Choose the preposition.
items.es: Under significa debajo de.

source.readingText: It is the last day of Pre-A1. Mia is on an adventure in the park. There is a big tree and there are two flowers. A small fox is under the tree. It can run fast. Mia likes animals, so she smiles. Her red ball is in her bag. She asks her friend Ben, “Where is the fox?” Ben says, “It is under the tree!” They are happy because they can use their English.

readingQuestions.question: What is in the park?
readingQuestions.answer: A big tree and two flowers
options: A big tree and two flowers

readingQuestions.question: How do Mia and Ben feel?

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Welcome to the Pre-A1 Grand Adventure! Listen to our story. Tom is in the garden. There is a tree and there are three flowers. A small dog is next to the tree. It can jump. Tom likes dogs. He has got a blue ball. The ball is under the chair. Tom asks, “Where is my ball?” His sister says, “It is under the chair!” Well done, Tom. You can use your English!

listeningQuestions.question: Who tells Tom where the ball is?
Which structures are reviewed in the story?
